Example subset of the World Flora Online taxonomic backbone (Plant List 2026-06)

Source: R/data.R
WFO.example2026.Rd

A small extract of the WFO Plant List 2026-06, used in the examples. It contains the names of the examples, the edge cases discussed in WFO.match() (a truncated genus, a species transferred to another genus, a local name) and every accepted name that these names refer to. For real work, download the complete backbone with WFO.download().

Usage

WFO.example2026

Format

A data.frame with 48 rows and the 12 columns read by WFO.read(core.only = TRUE): taxonID, scientificName, scientificNameAuthorship, taxonRank, taxonomicStatus, nomenclaturalStatus, acceptedNameUsageID, family, genus, specificEpithet, verbatimTaxonRank and infraspecificEpithet. As in the 2026-06 release, ranks are written in full and in lower case ("species", "variety"), and hybrids as "Mentha × piperita".

Source

The World Flora Online Consortium et al. (2026). World Flora Online Plant List June 2026. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20782718

Examples

data(WFO.example2026)
WFO.example2026[, c(
  "scientificName", "taxonomicStatus",
  "acceptedNameUsageID"
)]
